label: third original token when the second original token is digit 0
explanation: Fires at step t=2 of the original phase when the previous input (orig(1)) was the digit 0; this accounts for 99.7% of activation mass. Never fires in the delimiter or copy phases, and never after a 0 at later positions. The current token (orig(2)) barely matters. Magnitude depends on the first token: b gives the max, x/y/p/r give mid values, n/u/s give low values, and t/v often give zero (these are the main false positives). The only misses are near-zero activations at t=1 when orig(0)=0 (about 0.3% of mass).

issues: The miss attribution is slightly wrong. Misses at t=1 when orig(0)=0 are numerous (about 3.3k steps) but hold only about 0.02% of mass. The other roughly 0.2% of missed mass is at t=3, mostly when orig(1)=0 and orig(2)=0, e.g. 'm 0 0 q' fires 0.05 at step 3. Scores for t==3 & orig(1)==0 & orig(2)==0: precision 0.25, mass recall 0.0018. So 'only misses are at t=1' and 'never after a 0 at later positions' are slightly overstated. Both effects are tiny.

The false positives are fully systematic and match the explanation: with orig(0) in {t, v}, the predicate is 83% inactive (precision 0.17 on 1168 predicted steps). Excluding them raises test precision to 1.0.
The core claims check out: no activity in the delimiter or copy phases, 99.7% of mass at t=2, orig(0)=b is always active (precision 1.0).
